Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: num
- Register: "R049/2006-NL1-2013.01 Rev. 9"
- Document: "R49-1/2006-NL1-13.01"

The document itself says: "Number R49-1/2006-NL1-13.01 revision 9"

The register says "R049/2006-NL1-2013.01 Rev. 9".

Also there's a comment in the document context: "num: R049/2006-NL1-2013.01 Rev. 9" — that matches the register exactly.

So we have two forms of the certificate number:
- "R049/2006-NL1-2013.01 Rev. 9"
- "R49-1/2006-NL1-13.01"

Breaking down:
- R049 vs R49: leading zero, same recommendation R 49 (Continuously operated dynamic measuring systems for liquids). Same entity, format drift.
- /2006 vs -1/2006: R049/2006 vs R49-1/2006 — the "-1" indicates part 1 of the recommendation (Measuring systems for...). OIML certificates often have part numbers like "R49-1" for the recommendation part. The register's form "R049/2006-NL1-..." hmm.
- NL1: issuing authority (Netherlands, NMi = NL1).
- 2013.01 vs 13.01: year shorthand 13 = 2013. Same entity, format difference.
- Rev. 9 vs revision 9: same revision.

Also the source PDF filename: "r049-2006-nl1-2013-01-rev9.pdf" — matches register form (canonical).

Per rules: "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form."

So verdict: same-entity, best_value = "R049/2006-NL1-2013.01 Rev. 9" (register's canonical form).

Why: short sentence: The document's "R49-1/2006-NL1-13.01" is the same certificate with cosmetic formatting differences (leading zero, year shorthand 13 vs 2013, hyphen vs slash), and the register carries the canonical form matching the PDF filename and embedded cert_id comments.
